Register derived outcomes and named donor pools

Source: R/registry.R
registry.Rd

Extension points for data that a plain column cannot express. A specification names an outcome in data$outcome and a pool in pool$base; when the name is not a column (or "all"), sdidlab looks it up here.

Usage

register_outcome(name, fn, label = name, units = NA_character_)

register_pool(name, fn)

registered_outcomes()

registered_pools()

Arguments

name

The name specifications will use.

fn

The function, as described above.

label, units

For outcomes: how axes and tables should describe it.

Value

The name, invisibly.

Details

  • An outcome function takes (panel, spec) and returns a data frame with columns unit, time and y – for example a share computed from two columns, or a series built from another table.

  • A pool function takes (panel, spec) and returns either a character vector of donor units, or a data frame with columns unit, included (logical) and optionally reason, which is how a pool records why a candidate was left out.

Both receive the whole specification, so a spec's free-form options section can parameterise them. Registrations last for the R session; put them in a package's .onLoad() or at the top of a script.

Examples

register_outcome("packs_log", function(panel, spec) {
  d <- panel$data
  data.frame(unit = d[[panel$unit]], time = d[[panel$time]],
             y = log(d$PacksPerCapita))
}, label = "Log packs per capita")

register_pool("west", function(panel, spec) {
  c("Arizona", "Colorado", "Idaho", "Montana", "Nevada", "New Mexico",
    "Oregon", "Utah", "Washington", "Wyoming")
})

registered_outcomes()
#> [1] "packs_log"
registered_pools()
#> [1] "west"
